parts.name: nut_plate
parts.desc: Laser-cut 6061 nut plate under the carrier's square. How the bed is lifted (v12.1): the POM anti-backlash nut z_nut (supplied on the motor's screw; StepperOnline drawing A4003: 26 mm square flange, 4-M4 on an 18.5 mm square) rides lead screw leadscrew. Its flange is bolted to the underside of this 9.525 mm plate by four M4 x 12 through the flange's own holes into M4 threads tapped in the plate (drilled through the flange as a template by the builder); the plate is bolted under the 2020 square's member sq_rear (two M5 from below into T-nuts) and reaches 56.2 mm out to the screw. The nut is fixed: the screw, held only by its motor and free at its top end, bends slightly to follow any misalignment (as on a Voron Trident). The screw passes a 9 mm hole open to the plate's outer edge, so the plate slides onto a screw whose motor already stands.

parts.name: z_motor_plate
parts.desc: Z motor plate (v12.1 znut-direct): 6.35 mm 6061, outline true arcs; the motor hung under it by its pilot and four M3; two 8 mm holes over the posts (the M5's 10 mm washer covers them), so the plate (and the motor's screw) can be slid +/-1.25 mm to line up with the fixed nut at assembly (bed at the bottom of its travel, post bolts loose, then tightened).
